Print, summarize, compare and plot a fitted SPoRC model

Source: R/utils_s3_methods.R
sporc_fit.Rd

fit_model returns a list of class sporc_fit. Typing its name prints a short description of the fit in place of the whole list, summary() tabulates the estimates by parameter, and logLik() returns the maximized log likelihood, so AIC(fit_1, fit_2) compares fits. coef(), vcov() and confint() return the fixed effect estimates, their covariance matrix and their confidence intervals, and as.data.frame() returns one reported quantity as a long data frame. plot() draws one of the package's plots for this fit alone; to compare fits, call the plotting function itself with a list of them. The fit is still a list: fit$rep, fit$sd_rep and RTMB::sdreport(fit) work as before, and unclass(fit) prints every element.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sporc_fit'
print(x, digits = 6, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sporc_fit'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sporc_fit'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sporc_fit'
coef(object, random = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sporc_fit'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sporc_fit'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sporc_fit'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  what,
  labels = list(),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'sporc_fit'
plot(x, type = "ts", model_name = "Model 1", ...)

Arguments

x

A fit returned by fit_model.

digits

Number of significant digits printed for the objective and the largest absolute gradient. Default 6.

...

For plot, further arguments of the plotting function, such as do_ci, Selex_Type, year_indx or data_source. Not used by the other methods.

object

A fit returned by fit_model.

random

For coef, TRUE returns the random effects with the fixed effects, in the order RTMB stores them. Default FALSE.

parm

For confint, which estimates to return: parameter names (every estimated value of each, e.g. "ln_RecDevs") or positions in coef(object). Default is every fixed effect.

level

Confidence level for confint. Default 0.95.

row.names

Not used.

optional

Not used.

what

For as.data.frame, name of the quantity in x$rep to return, e.g. "SSB" or "NAA".

labels

For as.data.frame, optional named list of labels for populations, regions, seasons, sexes and fleets, as in label_dims.

type

Which plot to draw, each from the function named: "ts" (the default, get_ts_plot, which needs do_sdrep = TRUE), "selex" (get_selex_plot), "biological" (get_biological_plot), "data_fitted" (get_data_fitted_plot), "nLL" (get_nLL_plot), "idx_fits" (get_idx_fits_plot), "catch_fits" (get_catch_fits_plot) or "at_age_fits" (get_at_age_fits_plot).

model_name

Name the fit is given in the plot legend. Default "Model 1".

Value

plot returns what the plotting function returns, a ggplot or a list of them. print returns the fit invisibly. summary returns a data frame with one row per parameter name: Par, Type ("fixed" or "random"), N (number of estimated values), Est_Min and Est_Max (range of the estimates, on the scale the parameter is estimated on), SE_Max (largest standard error) and Abs_Grad_Max (largest absolute gradient, NA for random effects). get_par_est_info gives one row per estimated value. logLik returns minus the objective the fit minimized, with df the number of estimated fixed effects. That objective includes every penalty and prior in the model, and with random set it is the marginal. No number of observations is set, so BIC() is not available. coef returns the fixed effect estimates on the scale each is estimated on (mostly log), named by parameter, so a name repeats once per estimated value. vcov returns their covariance matrix from the sdreport, and confint a matrix of lower and upper limits on that same scale, the estimate plus and minus a normal quantile times its standard error. Both need do_sdrep = TRUE and leave out random effects, whose standard errors are in fit$sd_rep. as.data.frame returns one row per value of the quantity, with a column for each dim (Region, Year, Age, ...) and the value in value. A fit run with do_optim = FALSE has no estimates, and summary, logLik, coef and confint stop on it.

Details

print says whether nlminb converged and gives the largest absolute gradient at the estimates, both stored with every optimized fit. The Hessian check and the standard errors are read from $sd_rep, so they are shown only for a fit run with do_sdrep = TRUE.

See also

Other Utility: fit_model(), get_logistN_Sigma(), get_par_est_info(), label_dims(), post_optim_sanity_checks(), rho_trans(), set_data_indicator_unused()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit <- fit_model(data, parameters, mapping, do_sdrep = TRUE)
fit
summary(fit)
AIC(fit)
coef(fit)
confint(fit, parm = "ln_global_R0")
ssb_df <- as.data.frame(fit, what = "SSB") # columns Pop, Region, Year, value
plot(fit, type = "selex")
} # }
